result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B clearly flags every assumption, including title tracking, label values, placeholder colors, button line-height, hover style and breakpoints, and gathers them into a confirm list for the designer. Its line-height ratios are precise, and it mentions font-display: swap and checking the fallback font. A is richer on responsive behavior (no fluid scaling, 65ch measure, text-wrap, a 320px test) and on link states, but it doesn't mark the title tracking as proposed and rounds 28/22 to 1.275. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover every style in a clear table with rem values and unitless line heights. A marks every value it had to fill in (title tracking, label specs, colours, breakpoints) as [CONFIRM] and lists them at the end, and its checklist tells the dev to check the fallback fonts. B adds more on spacing, wide-screen behaviour and link states, but it presents the title tracking and the 'no fluid scaling' choice as decided rather than proposed, and it never says what to check if Inter fails to load.
